conventions: TypeScript strict mode everywhere; no `any` except where the surrounding code already casts (e.g. untrusted input in restore.ts is typed `unknown` and narrowed).
Formatting is prettier through eslint-plugin-prettier (80 columns, double quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent); the eslint check runs `--fix` first, so never hand-align code.

Import groups, separated by blank lines: external packages, then `@excalidraw/*` value imports, then `import type` blocks, then relative imports. Across packages import through the `@excalidraw/common` / `@excalidraw/element` / `@excalidraw/element/types` aliases; inside `packages/element/src` import siblings relatively (`./textStyleRanges`). Type-only imports use `import type`.

Elements are immutable by convention: change them only through `newElementWith(el, updates)` or `scene.mutateElement(el, updates)` so `version`/`versionNonce` bump; a `styleRanges` change always writes a brand-new array of brand-new range objects, never an in-place edit.
Text style offsets are UTF-16 code-unit offsets into `originalText` (the same units as `textarea.selectionStart`), half-open `[start, end)`.
A stored range object carries only the style keys that are set: `color` and/or `backgroundColor` are omitted when unset, never `null` or `undefined` in stored data.
Every colour painted on canvas or written to SVG goes through `applyDarkModeFilter(color, theme === THEME.DARK)` (canvas: `renderConfig.theme`; SVG: `renderConfig.theme`).
SVG nodes are created with `svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, name)` and filled with `setAttribute` / `textContent`; never the global `document`, never string-built markup.
User-facing strings go through `t("labels.<key>")`; new keys are added to `packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json` only.

Tests use vitest globals (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi`). jsdom editor tests render `<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />`, drive it with `API`, `Keyboard`, `UI`, `getTextEditor`, `updateTextEditor`, wrap state changes in `act`, read state from `window.h` (`h.elements`, `h.state`, `h.app`), and assert with `toEqual` / `toBe` on explicit values, not snapshots.
No new dependencies; never touch `package.json`, `yarn.lock` or `packages/excalidraw/types/**`.

decisions.choice: Offsets index `originalText`. Wrapping, re-measuring, font changes and container resizes rewrite only `text`, so ranges never move for them; renderers map ranges onto wrapped lines at draw time with `getTextStyleLineRuns`.
rejected: Offsets into wrapped `text` (every re-wrap would have to remap ranges)
decisions.reason: Gate 1 default; `originalText` is exactly the textarea value, so selection offsets need no translation and wrapping cannot drift ranges.

decisions.choice: `ExcalidrawTextElement.styleRanges?: readonly TextStyleRange[]` with `TextStyleRange = Readonly<{ start: number; end: number; color?: string; backgroundColor?: string }>`, declared in `packages/element/src/types.ts`. Omit-when-empty: the key exists on an element only when it holds at least one range. `newTextElement` writes it only when the clamped input has a range; `restore.ts` writes it only when sanitising leaves a range (and strips any incoming key otherwise); App.text.ts and the colour actions remove the key with `withoutStyleRanges` when an edit or a clear leaves no range. A stored `styleRanges` is never `[]`. Readers treat a missing (or `undefined`) field as no ranges.
rejected: Always present, `[]` by default (changes every created/restored text element and every committed snapshot that serialises one, breaking NFR-1 byte-identity and the frozen file scope)
A required field (breaks every text-element literal and skeleton in the repo and in host apps)
`null`-valued style keys (larger JSON, two spellings of unset)
decisions.reason: Gate 2 instruction: every existing element, scene and snapshot stays byte-identical; same optional-field precedent as `labelPosition?`.

decisions.choice: `AppText.handleTextWysiwyg`'s `updateElement` (App.text.ts) computes `shiftRangesForEdit(element.styleRanges, element.originalText, nextOriginalText)` for every onChange and onSubmit, and writes `styleRanges` only when the helper returns a different reference.
rejected: Shifting inside textWysiwyg's oninput with a caret hint (jsdom and programmatic value changes leave the caret at the end, and paste/indent/normalisation paths bypass it)
decisions.reason: One code path already receives the before and after `originalText` for typing, paste, indent, IME and submit; a common-prefix/suffix diff is exact for every edit except inserts that repeat a neighbouring character, where the result renders identically.

decisions.topic: Insert / delete semantics at range boundaries
decisions.choice: Splice (offset o, deleted d, inserted i): start' = start < o ? start : start >= o + d ? start - d + i : o + i; end' = end <= o ? end : end >= o + d ? end - d + i : o; a range with start' >= end' is removed; the result is normalised. So an insert exactly at a range start shifts it, an insert exactly at its end does not extend it, an insert strictly inside grows it.
rejected: Extending a range when typing at its end (rich-editor style)
decisions.reason: Deterministic and matches FR-3 wording (before shifts, inside grows, across trims, after untouched).

decisions.topic: Exposing the textarea selection to actions
decisions.choice: `packages/excalidraw/actions/colorTargets.ts` holds a per-app registry (`WeakMap` keyed by the App instance) of a live selection source `{ elementId, read() }`, registered by `textWysiwyg` when the editor opens and cleared on cleanup, plus a listener set notified on selection-changing events. Actions call `getTextEditorSelection(app, appState)` at perform time; the highlight picker subscribes through `subscribeToTextEditorSelection`.
rejected: A new AppState field (packages/excalidraw/types.ts and appState.ts are outside the allowlist and every appState snapshot would churn)
Querying `.excalidraw-wysiwyg` from the DOM inside actions (breaks with several editors on a page)
decisions.reason: Reads the selection at execution time (never a stale render closure, per resolveColorTarget's rule) and needs no React state for the textarea.

decisions.topic: Stroke colour with a text selection
decisions.choice: While `getTextEditorSelection` returns a non-empty selection, `actionChangeStrokeColor` writes the colour to that range only: element `strokeColor`, sticky-note ink and the `currentItem*` defaults are left unchanged. Picking a colour equal to the element's `strokeColor` clears the range's `color`. With no selection or no open editor the existing code path runs untouched.
decisions.reason: FR-8; clearing on the element colour keeps the data minimal and lets the run follow later element-colour changes.

decisions.choice: New action `actionChangeTextHighlight` (name `changeTextHighlight`, in actionProperties.tsx) whose PanelComponent renders the new `TextHighlightPicker`: a strip of five swatches from `DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS` (`transparent` clears the highlight). It renders only while a text is being edited with a non-empty textarea selection, in the full and compact styles panels (not the mobile bar). Value shape `{ color: string | null }`; `null` or a transparent colour clears `backgroundColor`.
rejected: Reusing `ColorPicker` with type `elementBackground` (its popup state collides with the background picker shown alongside it)
decisions.reason: Gate 1 default: a new compact highlight picker shown only while editing with a selection.

decisions.choice: `getTextStyleLineRuns(text, originalText, ranges)` walks the lines of `text` and aligns each to `originalText` without measuring: after a line ending at offset c, if `originalText` from c to its next `\n` is whitespace only, the next line starts after that `\n` (hard break), otherwise at the first non-whitespace character at or after c (soft break, trimmed whitespace skipped). If any line is not found at its aligned offset it returns `null`, and both renderers draw the element exactly as today.
decisions.reason: O(n), no width needed (the wrap width is not stored), and a safe fallback for legacy or out-of-sync `text`.

decisions.choice: When `isRTL(element.text)` is true both renderers skip per-run drawing and draw the element exactly as today (ranges stay stored).
decisions.reason: Per-run left-to-right placement is wrong for bidi text; out of scope to lay out bidi runs.

decisions.choice: `textWrapping.ts`, `textElement.ts`, `textMeasurements.ts`, `mutateElement.ts`, `delta.ts`, `data/reconcile.ts`, `actions/actionStyles.ts` and `actions/register.ts` are not edited. Delta compares top-level props shallowly and stores the whole array as the replaced value; reconcile is whole-element last-writer-wins; paste-styles copies an explicit property list that excludes `styleRanges`; `register()` already registers any action defined in actionProperties.tsx.
decisions.reason: Offsets on `originalText` make wrapping/refresh no-ops for ranges; the jsdom tests pin undo/redo, reconcile and paste-styles behaviour instead.

decisions.choice: A colour is kept only when it is a string of 1 to 64 characters matching `/^[#a-z0-9(),.%\s/-]+$/i` and not containing `url(` (case-insensitive); otherwise the whole range entry is dropped.
decisions.reason: NFR-7: only plain colour syntax ever reaches an SVG `fill` attribute.

decisions.choice: None expected: with omit-when-empty no existing element gains a key, so no committed snapshot changes. units.behaviour: Pure helpers for styled ranges: normalise, clamp, shift on edits, apply a style to a span, sanitise untrusted input, split wrapped text lines into styled runs, and drop an emptied `styleRanges` key from an element.
rules: 1. Import only `import type { TextStyleRange } from "./types";` — no other imports, no side effects, no mutation of inputs; every function returns new arrays of new range objects (except the documented same-reference returns of shiftRangesForEdit).

2. Export `type TextStyleUpdate = { color?: string | null; backgroundColor?: string | null }` (key absent: keep; `null`: clear; string: set) and `type TextStyleRun = { text: string; color: string | null; backgroundColor: string | null }`.
3. A style value counts as set only when it is a non-empty string; when building a range copy only the set keys (`color`, `backgroundColor`) onto the new object, never write `null`/`undefined` keys.

4. normalizeRanges(ranges): drop entries whose start/end are not finite numbers, whose start >= end, or with no set style; copy kept entries; sort by start then end (stable); when an entry starts before the previous kept entry's end, move its start to that end and drop it if now empty; merge an entry into the previous one when previous.end === entry.start and both `color` and `backgroundColor` are equal (both unset counts as equal); always return a new array.
5. clampRanges(ranges, textLength): map start/end to `Math.min(Math.max(value, 0), textLength)`, then return normalizeRanges of the result.

6. shiftRangesForSplice(ranges, offset, deletedCount, insertedCount) with o = offset, d = deletedCount, i = insertedCount: start' = start < o ? start : start >= o + d ? start - d + i : o + i; end' = end <= o ? end : end >= o + d ? end - d + i : o; drop ranges with start' >= end'; return normalizeRanges of the result.

7. shiftRangesForEdit(ranges, prevText, nextText): return `ranges` itself (same reference, possibly undefined) when ranges is undefined or empty or prevText === nextText; otherwise p = common prefix length, s = common suffix length capped at Math.min(prevText.length, nextText.length) - p, and return shiftRangesForSplice(ranges, p, prevText.length - p - s, nextText.length - p - s).

8. applyStyleToRange(ranges, start, end, style): with start = Math.max(0, start), if start >= end return normalizeRanges(ranges). Otherwise split every range at start and end: pieces outside [start, end) keep their style; pieces inside get the merged style (per key: undefined keeps the range's value, null removes it, a string sets it); every gap inside [start, end) not covered by a range becomes a new piece carrying only the string values of `style`; return normalizeRanges of all pieces (which drops unstyled pieces and merges equal neighbours).

9. sanitizeTextStyleRanges(input: unknown, textLength): non-array input returns []. Keep an entry only if it is a non-null object, `start` and `end` are integers (Number.isInteger) with start < end, and each of `color`/`backgroundColor` is absent, null, or a valid colour (string of 1 to 64 chars matching /^[#a-z0-9(),.%\s/-]+$/i and not matching /url\s*\(/i); an entry with an invalid colour is dropped whole; an entry with no valid style is dropped. Build fresh range objects from the kept fields and return clampRanges(kept, textLength).

10. getTextStyleLineRuns(text, originalText, ranges): return null when ranges is undefined or empty. Clamp ranges to originalText.length. Split `text` on "\n". Line 0 starts at offset 0. For each later line, with c = end offset of the previous line: let nl = originalText.indexOf("\n", c); if nl !== -1 and originalText.slice(c, nl) is whitespace only, the line starts at nl + 1; otherwise it starts at the first index >= c whose character does not match /\s/. If originalText.startsWith(line, lineStart) is false, return null.

11. For each aligned line [lineStart, lineStart + line.length), emit runs covering the whole line in order: consecutive segments between range boundaries clipped to the line, each `{ text, color, backgroundColor }` with unset styles as null; merge adjacent segments with equal styles; a line with no styled character (including an empty line) yields exactly one run `{ text: line, color: null, backgroundColor: null }`. Advance through the sorted ranges with a moving index so the whole call is O(lines + ranges).

12. withoutStyleRanges(element): return `element` itself (same reference) when it has no own `styleRanges` key (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`); otherwise return a shallow copy without that key (destructure `{ styleRanges: _, ...rest }`), with no version bump — callers pass the result to `newElementWith`.

13. Give every export a one-paragraph JSDoc stating the offset base (`originalText`) and the boundary semantics of rule 6; withoutStyleRanges' JSDoc states the omit-when-empty rule (a stored `styleRanges` is never `[]`).

units.behaviour: SVG export writes styled lines as `<tspan>` runs with per-run `fill`, preceded by a `<rect>` per highlighted run; unstyled text exports byte-identically.
rules: 1. Add `getFontString,` to the `@excalidraw/common` import after `getFontFamilyString,`; add `import { getLineWidth, getTextStyleLineRuns } from "@excalidraw/element";` after the `getLineHeightInPx` import.

2. Replace only the per-line `for` loop. Before it: `const lineRuns = direction === "ltr" && element.styleRanges?.length ? getTextStyleLineRuns(lines.join("\n"), element.originalText, element.styleRanges) : null;` and `const font = getFontString(element);` (only used for styled lines).

3. Per line: build the `<text>` node with exactly today's attributes in today's order (x, y, font-family, font-size, fill, text-anchor, style, direction, dominant-baseline). If the line's runs are missing or all unstyled, set `textContent = lines[i]` as today and append it.

4. For a styled line: lineWidth = getLineWidth(lines[i], font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment); x0 = horizontalOffset - lineWidth * (textAlign center ? 0.5 : right ? 1 : 0). For each run with a backgroundColor, create a `rect` (svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "rect")) with x = x0 + width of the preceding runs, y = i * lineHeightPx, width = getLineWidth(run.text, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment), height = lineHeightPx, fill = applyDarkModeFilter(run.backgroundColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK), and append it to `node` before the line's `<text>`.

5. Then give the `<text>` one `tspan` child per run (createElementNS(SVG_NS, "tspan")), `textContent = run.text`, attribute `fill` = applyDarkModeFilter(run.color ?? element.strokeColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK), and append the `<text>` to `node`.
6. All values are set with setAttribute/textContent; no markup strings.

units.behaviour: Restoring a text element writes a sanitised `styleRanges` only when at least one valid range survives; legacy input, an empty list and fully corrupt input restore with no `styleRanges` key.
rules: 1. Import `sanitizeTextStyleRanges` and `withoutStyleRanges` from `@excalidraw/element` in one import on its own line after the `refreshTextDimensions` import.

2. After the `lineHeight` const in `case "text"`, compute `const styleRanges = sanitizeTextStyleRanges(element.styleRanges, (element.originalText || text).length);` so the clamp length is that of the restored originalText.

3. Pass `withoutStyleRanges(element)` instead of `element` as the first argument of that restoreElementWithProperties call, because it spreads the raw input first and would otherwise carry an unsanitised or empty `styleRanges` through; the `extra` expressions keep reading `element`.

rules: 1. Imports: `Excalidraw` from `../index`; `API` from `./helpers/api`; `Keyboard`, `Pointer`, `UI` from `./helpers/ui`; `getTextEditor`, `updateTextEditor` from `./queries/dom`; `act`, `render`, `unmountComponent`, `fireEvent`, `screen` from `./test-utils`; `actionChangeStrokeColor`, `actionChangeTextHighlight`, `actionChangeFontFamily` from `../actions/actionProperties`; `actionCopyStyles`, `actionPasteStyles` from `../actions/actionStyles`; `restoreElements` via `import * as restore from "../data/restore"`; `reconcileElements` and type `RemoteExcalidrawElement` from `../data/reconcile`; `exportScene` from `../scene/export`; `getDefaultAppState` from `../appState`; `CaptureUpdateAction`, `getTextStyleLineRuns`, `newElementWith`, `newTextElement` from `@excalidraw/element`; `FONT_FAMILY`, `KEYS` from `@excalidraw/common`.
2. Call `unmountComponent()` at module level; in `beforeEach` render `<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />` and `API.setElements([])`; `const { h } = window;`.

3. Open an editor on a new text with `UI.clickTool("text")`, `mouse.clickAt(20, 30)`, `const editor = await getTextEditor()`, `updateTextEditor(editor, "hello world")`; select with `editor.setSelectionRange(6, 11)` then `fireEvent.select(editor)`; run actions inside `act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(action, "ui", value))`.

4. Read the edited element as `h.elements.find(isTextElement)` (import `isTextElement` from `@excalidraw/element`; latest object), never a stale reference; create the pointer with `const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");`.

5. "No ranges" on a created or restored element is asserted as key absence, `expect(el).not.toHaveProperty("styleRanges")` — never `toEqual([])`, which would also pass for a stored empty array. No test uses snapshots (`toMatchSnapshot`/`toMatchInlineSnapshot`).
